bridge_result_bank_caveat: An operand that is a produced plane must be read from the result bank, and the bridge names one output per bank that may do so. Only m0 and m1 have one, and m2_rd_en is forced low for every mapped operator, so even an operation whose leg is otherwise complete cannot read a third produced operand -- VECTOR.INDEX_SCORE's query, key and head-weight planes are all three arena-resident.
critical_path: HYPER_CONNECT_PRE is the first refusal in both DeepSeek graphs, so it is the whole critical path until it is done -- and its engine is ot_a3_hc_pre_t1_descriptor_rne.sv, already synthesizable and already qualified against both stores' shipped descriptors (results/rtl/a3_hc_pre_t1_campaign.json: 1,379,450 checks per simulator, dual-simulator agreement, ROM/HBM output parity, all 74 numeric boundary words exact). The remaining work is a bridge connection, not arithmetic: admit the operation, route to that engine, and emit its 8 weight and 16 combination words -- both register bundles, so the BIASED_TOPK two-pass emit applies rather than needing a second physical write port.

blocker.and_those_instances_are_superseded: The campaign binds deployment sha256 34ca189c... which is on disk as build/abi3/deepseek-v4-flash-rom-PRE-AM-E9. The current shipped ROM deployment is 3a240986... with 3,135 descriptors against that one's 3,405 -- 270 fewer at the same 1,323 instructions -- so AM-E9 removed descriptors and ids at or after the first removal shifted. The HBM deployment the campaign names is not on disk at all.

measured_2026_09_17.consequence: The connection work is much smaller than generalising 83 predicates. For the ROM store the engine's gates already match the shipped program and it can be connected as it stands. For HBM two constants are stale -- the operator id and, by the same shift, its wait set. Re-pinning them is a two-line change that would then be stale again after the next descriptor-count change, which is the argument for deriving both from the record instead; but it is not a blocker to a first token on ROM.

hbm.verdict: THE HBM PINNING HAS DRIFTED BY TWO. The first MHC operator is descriptor 547, not the 545 the engine gates on, so the engine would refuse the current HBM program at its instruction gate. The deployment the campaign names (ec7cff23...) is not on disk, so the drift cannot be attributed to a particular change here.

measured_2026_09_17.method: Both deployments rebuilt from the shipped graph at HEAD and every descriptor scanned for engine_family VECTOR with engine_sub MHC. The ROM rebuild reproduces the on-disk digest 3a240986..., so that deployment is current.
measured_2026_09_17.question: Do the HC_PRE engine's pinned descriptor constants still apply to the CURRENT shipped deployments? The engine gates on ROM program counter 15 / operator 381 / wait set 382 and HBM program counter 14 / operator 545 / wait set 546, and the campaign that qualified it binds a PRE-AM-E9 ROM deployment.

rom.verdict: THE ROM PINNING HOLDS COMPLETELY. Descriptor 381 is still the VECTOR.MHC operator, and the six views it names carry exactly the object ids, permissions and dtypes the engine's view gate pins. The engine would admit the current shipped ROM program as it stands.

view_gate.verdict: ALL SIX HOLD -- object id, permissions and dtype -- so the engine's whole ROM view gate is satisfied by the current shipped deployment, not just its operator id. dtype 16 is FMT_BF16 on the hidden stream and 18 is FMT_FP32 on the rest, which is what the gate expects.

blocker.what: ot_a3_vector_mhc_pre_tile_scheduler gates admission on 83 field comparisons across five gates, and they are pinned to two exact descriptor INSTANCES: ROM program counter 15 with operator descriptor 381 and wait set 382, HBM program counter 14 with operator 545 and wait set 546.
blocker.what_is_not_established_here: whether descriptor 381 still names the MHC operator in the current deployment. The count difference proves ids moved, not which ones; checking that is the first concrete step, and it decides whether the engine needs re-pinning against the current program or generalising outright.
blocker.which_constants_are_which: Of the 83, the dtypes, HC_EPSILON and the 256-bit contract digest ARE the operator's identity and should stay pinned. The program counters, operator and wait-set ids, and the per-store schedule tiling words 54..62 are properties of one build of one program and are what must be derived from the record instead. The datapath behind the gates already reads the record generically, which is the same shape as the frozen-admission-predicate pattern that froze Qwen3 at a fixed shape earlier in this work.

critical_path_detail.engine_status: finished and qualified, not connected. results/rtl/a3_hc_pre_t1_campaign.json passes over 1,379,450 checks per simulator with both simulators agreeing, all 74 numeric boundary words exact, ROM/HBM output parity and synthesizable elaboration. It emits the two results this kind needs -- 8 weight words and 16 combination words -- as register bundles, so the two-view problem is the BIASED_TOPK two-pass emit and not a second physical write port.

remaining_work.and_for_hbm: two constants are stale -- the MHC operator is descriptor 547 where the engine gates on 545 -- and the HBM view gate's object ids were not checked here, so that store needs the same measurement before it is connected.
remaining_work.then: admit VECTOR.MHC with the PRE form in the bridge, route to the engine, and emit its 8 weight and 16 combination words in two passes over the single result port, as ROUTE.BIASED_TOPK already does for two register-sourced views.
remaining_work.what: A semantic-record collector. The engine takes 128 words in one bundle and no existing module sees them all: the bridge holds the operator, numeric payload and resolved views but has ZERO mentions of the SCHEDULE descriptor, which is words 52..63; the microsequencer decodes that in S_SCHED_WAIT and the views arrive later from the resolver bank.
remaining_work.why_it_is_tractable: The operator descriptor names every piece by id -- input_view_0..3 370..373, output_view_0/1 375/377, schedule_id 379, numeric_profile_id 378 -- and the microsequencer already fetches descriptors by id. So the collector latches what the sequencer is already walking past rather than resolving anything itself.

second_staleness.consequence: Connecting the engine needs its schedule gate regenerated against the current descriptor as well as the id half fixed. That is a legitimate re-pin: unlike a descriptor id, tile geometry and bank masks ARE architectural facts the gate should check. The committed vectors were deliberately NOT overwritten here, because the RTL gate still expects the old ones and the committed campaign passes against them; replacing one without the other would leave neither meaning anything.
second_staleness.reading: A regenerated record reproduces descriptor 379 exactly. The committed vectors and the RTL schedule_rom gate agree with each other and both disagree with the descriptor, and the disagreement is not a renumbering -- a bank_mask of 0x40000000 and a port_mask of 56 are not plausible values for those fields, while 8 and 3 are. So the SCHEDULE encoding changed at some point and neither the vectors nor the gate were regenerated. This is a SECOND staleness, independent of the descriptor-id renumbering, and it is semantic rather than positional.
second_staleness.what: The engine gates on the SCHEDULE descriptor contents in words 52..63, and those are pinned to a superseded encoding. Word map: 54 issue_window, 55 tile_rows, 56 tile_cols, 57 tile_depth, 58 bank_mask, 59 port_mask, 61 resource_bound, 62 max_outstanding.

critical_path_detail.the_record_is_what_the_bridge_already_ho: The engine takes a 128-word semantic record: word 0 profile, word 1 active_tokens, words 2..9 the instruction, 10..32 the operator descriptor, 33..51 the numeric payload including the 256-bit contract digest, 52..63 the schedule, and six 10-word view records from word 64. Every one of those is a field the bridge latches already, so the connection is a packing function rather than new architecture.
critical_path_detail.why_first: It is the first refused kernel in both DeepSeek graphs -- index 4 of V4-Flash, index 3 of V4.1 -- and a refused operation raises TRAP_CAPABILITY, so nothing after it is reachable. Until it is wired it is the entire critical path.

forced_order_note: A refused operation stops the program, so no kernel after the first refusal is reachable and the program's own order fixes the order the work must be done in. The first entry is the whole critical path until it is done.
leg_qualification_harness: tools/run_a3_operator_admission_rtl_campaign.py anchors every case to a Qwen3 program counter and its golden write stream, so it cannot cover a leg for an operator Qwen3 does not issue -- which is all thirteen. Qualifying one leg at a time needs a single-operator vehicle that lowers a minimal graph naming one refused operator and checks it against that operator's reference; otherwise a leg is only exercisable once a whole DeepSeek program lowers, needing ten (V4-Flash) or thirteen (V4.1) legs at once.

statement: A kernel naming an operation the bridge refuses raises TRAP_CAPABILITY, so the admitted set is exactly the subset of this graph the RTL can execute -- except for the families the bridge does not execute at all, which are listed separately rather than counted as gaps. Every refused operation has a module in rtl/abi3, but a module is not a form match: the engine array carries two operands and one result per dispatch, and an operation asking for more needs that surface widened before an admission leg can be written. ot_a3_vector_convert.sv states its own restriction in its header. Nor is a module in the tree necessarily instantiated: five of the thirteen are in ot_a3_engine_array.sv and the rest are instantiated by nothing, so they need a place to run before a leg means anything.
